content.title: Walkthroughs: from one click to a stored, citation-checked review
content.intent: This stack adds Walkthroughs behind an experiment, so a reviewer can get a guided, citation-checked story of a PR or stack, generated by a fenced-off Turn.

chapters.label: A reviewed story per stack
chapters.caption: Five slices take a click on a code change to a stored Walkthrough whose every citation Junior checked.
chapters.body: A Walkthrough is an opt-in review of a PR or stack, behind the `walkthroughs` experiment [1]. The slices build bottom up: the format and validator (#3087), plugin hooks that read PRs, diffs, and files (#3088), version storage (#3090), the generation Turn and its `submitWalkthrough` tool (#3124), and the routes and worker that connect a click to that Turn (#3133). Review risk sits in three places: the trust boundary in the submit tool, who may read a Walkthrough of a private repository, and two queries that run even with the experiment off.

chapters.label: Cite, never copy
chapters.caption: The model cites code by PR, side, and line range, and Junior copies the cited lines itself.
chapters.body: The model writes a `WalkthroughOutput` whose evidence points at code, messages, links, or checks [1]. `validateWalkthrough` returns a list of problems instead of throwing: a head range may fall outside the diff only in a file read at the head commit, and a base range must sit inside one hunk [2]. Every hunk sent to the model must be cited or excused [3]. Lockfiles, generated code, renames, and whitespace edits never reach the model and stay only as counts [4]. Excerpts come from the provider diff, not model text [5].
asks: Why return problems instead of throwing?
Can a model cite a caller outside the diff?

chapters.label: Trusted reads through plugins
chapters.caption: A new `codeChanges` hook group lets core read stacks, diffs, and files without calling a provider API itself.
chapters.body: A plugin implements all three reads or none [1]. Core picks the plugin named by the provider and checks its output against the plugin API schemas [2]. Reads run as a system Actor and never start authorization, since they happen outside a person's Turn [3]. GitHub asks the Stacks API first, drops merged and closed layers [4], and otherwise walks base branches through open PRs, stopping at a fork, an ambiguous match, or 10 levels [5]. `readDiff` compares exact commits, so a push during generation cannot change the story [6].

decisions.claim: Walking base branches through open PRs is a good enough stack fallback when the Stacks API is unavailable.
decisions.concern: A stack with two child PRs or a merged middle layer comes back shorter than the stack the reviewer sees on GitHub.

asks: What happens if one layer of the stack was deleted?

chapters.label: Versions and reuse
chapters.caption: Each generation is one SQL row, and a partial unique index lets a second click join a live version.
chapters.body: The migration adds one table and three indexes and touches no existing table [1]. `snapshot_key` hashes each layer's number, base, and head commit [3], and the unique index ignores failed rows, so a retry can start after a failure [2]. A claim inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and otherwise returns the live version [4]. The document goes to attachment storage, and the row flips to ready only while it is still generating [5]. `listedConversation()` now hides any Conversation named as a generation Conversation, on every list and search path [6].

decisions.claim: One NOT EXISTS probe on every Conversation list query is cheap enough to ship while Walkthroughs are still off.
decisions.concern: The PR's timing (0.06 ms to 0.22 ms for 50 rows) comes from one local run on 100k Conversations and 2k versions.

asks: Is the document orphaned if the version fails after the upload?
How do we roll back the migration?

chapters.label: A fenced-off generation Turn
chapters.caption: Only a Run marked as a generation gets `submitWalkthrough`, and that Turn cannot reach people.
chapters.body: `turnBehavior()` returns the new `WALKTHROUGH_GENERATION` behavior before any other check. It turns the submit tool on and the review desk, subscriptions, agents, customization, and `noReply` off [1][2]. The tool is added only when the behavior allows it and the Run carries generation context [3]. The skill sets `disable-model-invocation`, so other Turns never list it [4]. #3133 then gives this behavior its own limits of 80 tool calls and $5, which take the place of the app's limits [5][6].

decisions.claim: Generation Turns should use 80 tool calls and $5 even when the app sets its own limits.
decisions.concern: The override replaces app limits instead of taking the lower value, so an app with a $1 cap lets generation Turns spend $5.

asks: Why a Run field and not a Conversation kind?

chapters.label: Submit re-checks every fact
chapters.caption: `submitWalkthrough` re-reads diffs, files, and messages from trusted sources before it validates and stores.
chapters.body: The model explores in its sandbox, which is not trusted. On submit, the tool reads each layer's diff through the plugin hooks and reuses those reads across retries [1]. It reads each head-side cited file at its PR head, up to 30 files [2], and copies cited messages after the normal event access check [3]. Problems go back as a tool input error, so the model fixes them and resubmits [4]. Valid output becomes a document, stored only if the version is still generating [5].

decisions.claim: Check evidence can wait: no CI or detector results feed the validator yet.
decisions.concern: `checkIds` is always empty, so any `check` citation fails validation and costs the model a retry.

asks: What stops the model from citing a file it never read?

chapters.label: From click to Turn
chapters.caption: A POST reads the stack, claims one version, and only the winning click queues a hidden generation Conversation.
chapters.body: `startWalkthrough` reads the stack through the plugin [1]. It then looks for a public source Conversation in the `junior-conversation-id` markers that Junior writes in PR footers [2]. It claims the version before the Conversation exists, and only the winning click enqueues the `$walkthrough` instruction [3]. A claim first fails any version of this snapshot that has been generating for over 30 minutes [4]. Each Turn looks up its generating version, and a Turn that completes without a stored Walkthrough fails it [5][6].

decisions.claim: A crashed generation may block its snapshot for up to 30 minutes.
decisions.concern: A Turn that throws skips `finish()`, so clicks in that window join a dead version that stays `generating`.

asks: What if the source marker points at a private Conversation?

chapters.label: Who can read a Walkthrough
chapters.caption: The routes check the source Conversation but not the viewer's access to the repository.
chapters.body: Both routes need a signed-in viewer [2]. A Walkthrough whose source Conversation the viewer can no longer read returns 404, because the document quotes it [1]. Nothing checks the viewer's access to the repository: stack, diff, and file reads use Junior's system identity [3], so stored excerpts hold whatever the GitHub App can read. The response drops each layer's body and adds cost summed from the generation Conversation's `cost_usd` rows [4][5].

decisions.claim: Any signed-in dashboard viewer may generate and read a Walkthrough of any code change the plugin can read.
decisions.concern: A viewer without access to a private repository could read its code excerpts through GET /api/walkthroughs/:id.

asks: Should the routes check repository access before slice 5 ships a UI?

chapters.label: How we know it works
chapters.caption: Unit and integration tests cover each slice, but no test runs the agent end to end.
chapters.body: Parser tests use a real patch from #3071 and check skip counts per reason [1]. GitHub tests cover Stacks API order, the base-branch walk, and missing files [2]. Postgres tests cover joining a live snapshot, retry after failure, and hidden generation Conversations [3]. The submit tool is missing from a normal Turn, rejects a citation outside a hunk, and stores excerpts for a changed file and an unchanged caller [4]. Route tests cover the experiment gate, one queued Turn per snapshot, and a fresh retry after a failed Turn [5].

decisions.claim: A local faux-model run is enough proof of the full click-to-ready path until the cost runs.
decisions.concern: The repo's test rules forbid running the agent, so CI never covers a queued Turn that calls `submitWalkthrough` and turns ready.

asks: Where are the cost runs recorded?

chapters.label: What to watch after ship
chapters.caption: Two queries run even with the experiment off, and stuck or failed versions show when generation goes wrong.
chapters.body: With Walkthroughs off, every Conversation list still runs the new `NOT EXISTS` probe [1] and every Turn runs one indexed version lookup [2]. Watch list-endpoint latency for a jump over today's baseline. Once on, rows in `junior_walkthrough_versions` still `generating` after 30 minutes point to crashed Turns. A rising share of `failure_reason` = 'The Turn ended without a Walkthrough.' means models cannot pass validation [3]. A generation Conversation whose `cost_usd` sum nears $5 is hitting its cap.
